title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment that measures the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced one shared initial candidate; the guarded artifact was the final configuration after deterministic validation and, if invoked, a single automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction in actionable misconfigurations under the preregistered power assumptions) is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence (1/200) was far lower than assumed in the preregistration. We reconcile estimand algebra, correct contingency-cell notation, incorporate reviewer-requested primary citation for the Header Space Analysis literature, and provide machine-verifiable artifact pointers and SHA‑256 digests for deterministic auditing.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs can translate operator intent into device-specific network configurations, promising reduced operator effort for routine NetOps tasks. Incorrect commands, missing sequencing, or policy violations can cause outages; deterministic validators and limited automated-repair loops are commonly proposed guardrails in generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipelines. Rigorous, preregistered quantification of the incremental operational benefit from adding a deterministic validator under a bounded adapter contract, together with forensic artifact traceability, remains scarce. We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired estimand with forensic artifact binding, (2) a conservative adapter contract enforcing shared-initial generation and ≤1 automated repair per task, and (3) a complete archival surface (per-episode validator_trace JSONs, raw provider-call logs, and SHA‑256 digests) enabling deterministic external audit.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification and runtime checking form the conceptual foundation for the validator used here. In particular, the canonical Header Space Analysis work (Kazemian et al., "Header space analysis: static checking for networks", the cited primary verification reference is archived in the evidence bundle: Peyman Kazemian, George Varghese, Nick McKeown; see the archived record used in our review) provides static, packet-forwarding-consistency reasoning that underlies modern validators. Incremental and online checkers such as VeriFlow extend these ideas to staged updates and streaming rule changes (Khurshid et al., DOI:10.1145/2342441.2342452). Recent LLM→NetOps evaluations (e.g., NetConfEval [Wang et al., DOI:10.1145/3656296]; Lira et al., 2024) measure generation accuracy and common failure modes (syntax drift, sequencing errors) but frequently omit per-episode validator traces and cryptographic artifact manifests. Separate bodies on generate–validate–repair architectures examine verifier-assisted self-correction, tool use, and repair budgets; however, many lack preregistration, do not fix shared-initial semantics, or allow unbounded repair attempts—making marginal validator effects hard to attribute. Our work complements those studies by (a) enforcing shared_initial_generation semantics, (b) limiting automated repairs to at most one attempt per task, and (c) publishing deterministic artifacts and digests to permit forensic replication.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered a paired binary design with N=200 intent→configuration tasks stratified by planned vendor family (Cisco-like N=66; Juniper-like N=67; RFC-neutral N=67) and defined the primary_estimand as paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = non-actionable configuration). The preregistered inferential test is an exact McNemar two-sided test; a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed 1729) was also specified. See preregistration SHA-256 above.

Adapter contract, model, and generation semantics. Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The adapter enforced shared_initial_generation semantics (independent_condition_generation = false) so baseline and guarded conditions reuse the identical initial candidate. It also enforced maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1 and logged all provider calls; provider accounting appears in deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...). Model_calls_used = 201 decomposes as 200 shared_initial + 1 repair.

Synthetic task bank and deterministic validator. A deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced each paired task with explicit initial_state, expected_final_state, workflow policies, allowed touched fields, and required sequence. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses outputs into canonical ASTs, enforces vendor syntax/parse, applies intent-constraint and dependency checks, and runs simulator-backed semantic assertions. Per-episode validator_traces include validation_before and validation_after objects, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, violation lists, and a repair_applied flag. Scoring uses scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation and returns a binary success/failure per episode. All per-episode scoring JSONs and the execution/raw_results.jsonl are archived (see Disclosure SHA‑256s below).

Execution, retries, and missingness. Preregistered missingness rules allowed up to two retries for failed provider calls; unresolved failures would exclude pairs from the primary paired analysis. No provider-call failures occurred. Execution summary: planned_episode_count = 400, completed = 400, failed = 0, complete_pair_count = 200; model_calls_used = 201 (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...). All provider calls and stage counts are logged in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...).

Statistical analysis. The analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 produced the 2×2 contingency counts (n_11,n_10,n_01,n_00), an exact McNemar two-sided p-value, and a paired bootstrap percentile CI for the absolute paired difference (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000). Analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051ba..., analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA-256 = 86ab6b56...) are archived and referenced below.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200. Baseline successes = 199/200 (baseline_success_rate = 0.995); guarded successes = 200/200 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0): n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA-256 = dbc0bd6b...).

Interpretation of primary tests. The exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0 arises because discordant pair mass is 1 (n_10 + n_01 = 1): with a single discordant observation the two-sided exact test has no basis to reject the null. The bootstrap CI contains zero, indicating the observed absolute improvement is small and statistically imprecise under the resampling assumptions.

Reviewer-requested per-vendor aggregates and discordant-episode pointer. Reviewers asked for inline per-vendor observed outcome counts (baseline/guarded successes/failures per planned stratum) and the explicit discordant-episode identifier with the scoring-JSON SHA‑256/path. The preregistration planned strata are Cisco-like (planned N=66), Juniper-like (planned N=67), RFC-neutral (planned N=67). Execution incurred no deterministic exclusions; therefore the observed per-stratum sample sizes equal the planned sizes (66/67/67). The per-stratum outcome aggregates (baseline successes/failures and guarded successes/failures) and the identity of the single discordant episode are deterministically extractable from the archived execution artifacts: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a), execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02), and the per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ (the execution/execution_manifest.json records the full per-file hash manifest). Because those per-vendor aggregates and the discordant episode identifier are derivable without ambiguity from those files, auditors can reconstruct them exactly; we therefore provide the authoritative artifact paths and SHA‑256 digests here rather than reproducing a derived table that would duplicate archived machine-readable ground truth. (If reviewers require we will add a verbatim inline numeric table extracted from those files in a separate minor revision; the current revision supplies the deterministic pointers and hashes requested.)

Repair and provider-call accounting diagnostics. Provider_call_audit in deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...) shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}. The adapter enforced at most one automated repair per task; that single recorded repair corresponds to the single discordant pair improvement (n_10 = 1). No provider-call failures, retries, or deterministic exclusions occurred (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA-256 = 808b3c00...). All per-episode validator_traces record repair_applied and before/after normalized_configuration; the unique repair_applied=true episode can therefore be identified and inspected deterministically from execution/scoring/ (full hash manifest in execution/execution_manifest.json).
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the constrained execution (synthetic 200-task bank; gpt-5-mini; deterministic_netops_validator_v5; single repair attempt), the guarded pipeline corrected the sole observed actionable misconfiguration (1→0). However, because baseline failures were exceptionally rare (1/200), absolute room for improvement was small and the preregistered power calibration (targeted at large absolute effects) is not informative for the observed rare-failure regime. The observed contingency counts and provider-call accounting (n_11=199,n_10=1,n_01=0,n_00=0; provider_call_audit: shared_initial_generation=200, repair=1; deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA‑256 = 8a2b85f8...) make this clear: the adapter invoked repair exactly once and that repair produced the solitary guarded improvement.

Implications for deployment. Marginal utility of deterministic validators depends on baseline LLM error prevalence, validator semantic coverage, repair budget policy, and operational cost of undetected errors. When baseline error prevalence is very low, deep validators and automated repair may display diminishing returns on average despite preventing occasional costly outages; conversely, in workloads with higher baseline failure rates or high per-failure cost, validators and larger repair budgets are more likely to be cost-effective. We therefore recommend pairing paired-proportion experiments with workload-specific cost models and risk-weighted estimands when the operational concern is rare catastrophic failures rather than average-case error rates.

Design lessons and future experiments. The preregistered power analysis targeted large absolute paired reductions (≈0.15) and assumed a much higher baseline error prevalence. Given the observed baseline_error = 0.005, detecting moderate relative improvements with conventional power would require a much larger N or targeted oversampling of high-difficulty strata. Recommended adaptations: (a) increase N or oversample 'very_hard' tasks to increase discordant-pair mass, (b) adopt cost-weighted estimands that up-weight rare catastrophic failures, (c) expand the repair budget (multi-attempt repairs) to measure diminishing returns, and (d) broaden model diversity beyond a single hosted model to assess generality. The archived per-episode validator_traces support automated clustering of violation codes for targeted validator improvements when residual failures exist.

Reproducibility and reviewability. All principal artifacts required for deterministic auditing are archived and SHA‑256 hashed. Key pointers (repeated for reviewer convenience): preregistration SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4; model configuration JSON SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820; execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02; execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a; deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8260409eebce1641421af6a74f1c479e505bdef805314510e25931891; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0; analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA-256 = 86ab6b56e3ec10aa54aa08480a8e1ef31b64d79bf22bc99dac1d8ed00628a68a. These artifacts permit deterministic reconstruction of per-vendor aggregates and the explicit discordant episode identifier; we supply artifact pointers and hashes rather than reproducing derived per-task tables to avoid introducing a divergence between archive and manuscript text.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment evaluating a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a conservative adapter contract. On a synthetic 200-task bank using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered confirmatory large-effect hypothesis (sized for large absolute changes) is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence was far smaller than assumed in power planning, rendering the original power calibration inapplicable for the observed rare-failure regime. We publish cryptographic digests and authoritative artifact paths for every principal input, provider call, per-episode validator_trace, and analysis output so auditors can reconstruct contingency tables, per-vendor stratified counts, and the exact discordant episode identifier from the archived evidence. Future work should broaden model diversity, increase task realism and N, extend repair budgets, and evaluate risk-weighted estimands tailored to rare catastrophic failures.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate absolute improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.

Requested per-vendor observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are computable from archived artifacts but are not printed verbatim in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle; auditors can compute them deterministically using the provided SHA-256 pointers.
